page: Amazon Web Services m6in.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The processor provides hardware acceleration instructions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA extensions. System memory is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached elastic storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier single-threaded compute, supported by a Geekbench single-core score of 1611.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1891.98. Hardware-assisted cryptographic routines also place within the median range, with PassMark CPU encryption measuring 3623.42. Because the instance operates on only two physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, multi-threaded throughput falls into lower percentiles, achieving 3433.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 3862.55 on stress-ng multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests yield 27.84 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.89 GB/sec for writes.

From an operational cost perspective, the m6in.xlarge provides balanced compute, memory, and network resources without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware or expensive local NVMe disks. The absence of integrated storage necessitates consideration of external EBS storage overhead. The hardware profile fits general-purpose production workloads that depend on steady network capacity rather than extreme parallel compute, including microservices, API backends, static web servers, application caching tiers, and mid-sized database frontends.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no GPU accelerators, using network-attached block storage for disk persistence. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields average single-core execution performance and reliable hardware cryptographic throughput, while multi-threaded scalability remains constrained by its physical two-core footprint. Delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the instance is engineered for medium-demand enterprise workloads such as web application hosting, lightweight caching layers, backend microservices, and general network-dependent services.
